parallel_frontier_algorithm.name: PLANNER_FRONTIER_V0_SAFE_SLICE
input_snapshot: declared context freshness and privacy/capability requirements
integration-consumption facts when WI-BIG-09 semantics exist
incident/vaccine planning facts when WI-BIG-13 semantics exist
steps: 1. Freeze one source snapshot identifier set; never mix dependency facts from different implicit moments.

2. Validate each node has a prepared JOB, stable logical identity, bounded mission, scopes, context inputs, critic requirements and return contract. Invalid/incomplete nodes are BLOCKED_CONTRACT_INCOMPLETE.
3. Ask only durable Campaign Controller facts whether the node's phase/gates permit planning now. Closed/unknown gates are BLOCKED_CAMPAIGN_GATE; Planner never opens them itself.

4. Evaluate every hard incoming edge. Missing RETURN/evidence/critic evidence blocks the node with explicit edge reason. A RETURN cannot satisfy REQUIRES_INTEGRATION unless the future WI-BIG-09 contract says so.
5. Validate required context revisions/freshness and project-root privacy/capability constraints. Unknown or incompatible required inputs block; do not silently downgrade scope.
6. The remaining nodes form the eligible set. Derive each inspectable unblock_vector from the DAG; preserve campaign_priority supplied by campaign authority.

7. Build a conflict graph over eligible nodes. Add a conflict when write scopes overlap, an exclusive authority target overlaps, a declared mutex exists, or one node requires the other's evidence. Read-scope overlap alone is not a conflict.

8. Deterministically order eligible nodes by campaign_priority descending, gate_critical true first, direct-dependents count descending, transitive-dependents count descending, then work_item_id ascending.

9. Greedily admit each ordered node to the frontier only if it conflicts with none already admitted. Record excluded-ready nodes as READY_DEFERRED_CONFLICT with the conflicting node/reason; do not relabel them blocked by dependency.
10. Emit frontier plus a derivation receipt containing graph revision, source snapshot refs, candidate/excluded nodes and reason codes. Identical durable inputs must replay to the same frontier.
11. Execution fabric may create dispatch/claim/run attempts for frontier nodes; it must not mutate the logical DAG identity or mission when doing so.

12. After new durable RETURN, campaign change, integration decision, incident signal or context freshness change, Planner recompiles from a new explicit snapshot rather than incrementally guessing hidden state.

frontier_output.frontier_id: Derived identifier tied to graph_revision_id + source_snapshot_refs.
frontier_output.deferred_ready: Eligible but mutually conflicting nodes with explicit conflict refs.
frontier_output.blocked: Nodes with typed reason codes and unsatisfied edge/input refs.
frontier_output.derivation_receipt: Replay inputs and deterministic ordering evidence.

falsifying_tests.assertion: Same graph revision + same durable source snapshot produces identical frontier and reason codes.
A predecessor RETURN alone never satisfies a REQUIRES_INTEGRATION edge while WI-BIG-09 semantics are unresolved.
A node with all worker dependencies complete remains blocked if Campaign Controller gate is closed or unknown.
Two READY nodes with overlapping non-commutative write scope never appear together in the same frontier.
Two dependency-independent nodes with overlapping read scope but disjoint write scope may appear together.
A required fresh independent critic cannot be satisfied by the original worker/run's own RETURN.
Retry/dispatch/run identifiers can change without changing the logical work_item_id or prepared mission.
Planner readiness, worker DONE and critic success cannot by themselves set Human Accepted, Current or Served.
Missing final incident/vaccine semantics yields an explicit pending/blocked hook where required rather than an invented policy.
